```plato
//==
// # Contact constraint rows
//
// A `ContactManifold3D` is what collision detection REPORTS: a body pair, a
// shared normal, the combined material, and however many points the pair test
// found. A `ContactConstraint3D` is what the solver ITERATES: one point, already
// paired with its bodies, already carrying the friction basis and the restitution
// target that were computed once at build time.
//
// The flattening is the point. Sequential impulses visit points, not manifolds,
// and every quantity that is constant across a solver iteration is hoisted into
// the row so that an iteration is arithmetic and nothing else:
//
//   * THE FRICTION BASIS IS STORED. Recomputing a tangent frame from the normal
//     each iteration is cheap but not stable: the two tangents an
//     orthonormalization picks can flip between iterations, and the accumulated
//     friction impulse is expressed in that basis, so a flip silently discards
//     it. Fixing the basis at build time is what lets friction accumulate.
//   * THE RESTITUTION TARGET IS STORED. Bounce is a function of the approach
//     speed BEFORE the solver runs. Reading it inside the loop would sample a
//     velocity the loop has already changed, and the bounce would decay with the
//     iteration count instead of being a property of the collision.
//   * THE ACCUMULATED IMPULSES ARE STORED, and they are the row's output as much
//     as the velocities are. Clamping the ACCUMULATED normal impulse to be
//     non-negative — rather than clamping each increment — is what lets a row
//     undo an over-correction made by a row solved earlier in the same pass, and
//     it is what makes the friction cone bound (mu times the accumulated normal
//     impulse) meaningful.
//
// `Flatten` builds these rows from manifolds and `WarmStartFrom` carries the
// accumulated impulses across a frame boundary; both are in
// `collision.library.plato`.

// One point of one contact, in the form the velocity solver iterates. BodyA and
// BodyB are indices into the solver's body array; Point is the world contact
// position in meters; Normal points from A toward B; Tangent and Bitangent
// complete a right-handed orthonormal frame with Normal and fix the friction
// basis for the life of the row; Penetration is the positive overlap depth;
// Friction is the combined dimensionless Coulomb coefficient and Restitution the
// combined bounciness in [0, 1]; TargetSeparationSpeed is the separation speed
// along Normal the solver aims for, in meters per second, already including
// restitution and already zero for a resting contact; and the three impulses are
// the accumulated solver output in newton-seconds along the three basis
// directions (all zero in a fresh row).
type ContactConstraint3D
    implements IValue
{
    BodyA: BodyIndex;
    BodyB: BodyIndex;
    Point: Point3D;
    Normal: Direction3D;
    Tangent: Direction3D;
    Bitangent: Direction3D;
    Penetration: Length;
    Friction: Number;
    Restitution: Proportion;
    TargetSeparationSpeed: Number;
    NormalImpulse: Impulse;
    TangentImpulse: Impulse;
    BitangentImpulse: Impulse;
}
```
